acceptanceCriteria: Attempt-bound typed decision/infrastructure/scope/blocked requests replace prose-based parking decisions and expose age/open status.
Infrastructure retries are bounded and do not park for human decision; existing debt/exhaustion/ownership rules remain authoritative.
Typed answers close the matching request and are delivered to the next worker; stale or conflicting answers are refused and tested.
Required contract, independent review, focused qualification, CEM/OCM, current-main integration and native completion/readback/audit are retained.
body:
Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/502; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Workers escalate by writing `NEEDS OPERATOR:` into a status file. There is no type, so infrastructure failures and real decisions look the same. In practice most escalations were claim/queue timeouts (#494), which parked tickets and made workers set `needs-human`, while real product-scope questions were mixed in. The operator has to read files to tell them apart, and nothing clears the request when it is answered.

## Request
`corvint-tasks ticket escalate --attempt A --kind decision|infrastructure|scope|blocked --question "..." [--options a,b]` and `ticket answer --target T --text ...`:
- `infrastructure` escalations are retried by the dispatcher (bounded) and never park the ticket;
- `decision`/`scope` appear in `dispatch status` and a queryable list, and an answer is delivered to the next worker through the claim result (see the ticket-note request);
- the park decision uses the kind, and open escalations carry age so stale ones are visible.

## Workaround in use
A steward script greps first lines for claim/timeout wording, removes the line, resets the state and tells the worker to retry.
